- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.0) — model tends to overshoot early in upward trends.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (negative sentiment < -0.3) — model underreacts to downward momentum, especially after sharp drops.
- Lag in price correction: model often delays reacting to sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment turns negative, forecast remains high for 2–3 days.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs and fails to adjust downward when sentiment turns negative, especially in 30-day horizon.
- Overshoot after spikes: model overreacts to sudden price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1–2 days) and forecasts higher than true outcome, especially in 30-day horizon.
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: if sentiment > 0.1, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for next 3 days; if sentiment < -0.3, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for next 3 days.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to overconfidence in short-term momentum — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
